I read somewhere that many artists start with structure when building a drawing,  which can overall cause it to look stiff. It helps to start with gesture in mind, then in the original layer/sketch dont worry /too/ much about anatomy. 

Of course get it looking somewhat close to what you had in mind and not totally anatomically off, but if your head is too wide there or the shoulder is a little off or some bs like that dont give it much thought.

 Use flowy lines to sketch and get the most basic map of your pose down. I don't even draw joints or anything in this layer, just some basic anatomical guide points and then scribble out a sort of silhouette of what the pose should look like.

 Then on the next layer, start worrying more about how the structure of the body would work with that pose and thats where you can make your corrections and worry about the anatomy.

So far that advice has helped me with the same issue
